description.value: A behavioural and voxel-based morphometry study of humour processing in patients with bvFTD and semantic dementia compared with healthy older individuals.

spans.text: Here we investigated humour processing and its neuroanatomical correlates in a cohort of patients with bvFTD and SD as well as healthy older individuals.

value: syndromes of bvFTD and SD are associated with impaired humour comprehension with differentiable neuropsychological deficits linked to the processing of novelty and familiarity respectively, in humorous scenarios.
patients with bvFTD would have particular difficulty processing less familiar scenarios
patients with SD might show a more general loss of humour comprehension extending across both familiar and novel scenarios.

spans.text: we hypothesised that syndromes of bvFTD and SD are associated with impaired humour comprehension with differentiable neuropsychological deficits linked to the processing of novelty and familiarity respectively, in humorous scenarios.

humour decision task

description.value: A forced-choice decision about whether non-verbal cartoons were intended to be humorous.

spans.text: a forced-choice decision (whether or not the scenario was intended to be humorous)
Four conditions were combined in a factorial design comprising cartoons that were intended to be either humorous or non-humorous and to represent familiar or novel scenarios.
Stimuli were presented on the monitor screen of a notebook computer running Matlab7 ® .

instructions.value: Decide whether or not the cartoon was intended to show ‘a joke’.

spans.text: The task on each on trial was to decide whether or not the cartoon was intended to show ‘a joke’ with a single ‘Yes/No’ response.

stimuli.value: Non-verbal cartoons without captions, depicting human and/or animal characters interacting with each other or the physical environment.

spans.text: All were line drawings without captions, each comprising a single frame depicting human and/or animal characters interacting with each other or with the physical environment.
with a single ‘Yes/No’ response
